mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2% annualized over the past 3 months signals inflationary pressure, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL annualized increase exceeds 2% and FEDFUNDS subsequently rise.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points within a month signals a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where UNRATE rises by more than 0.5pp within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where RSAFS declines for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals strengthening supply-side fundamentals, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where INDPRO increases by more than 1% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payroll employment (PAYEMS) for three consecutive months signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where PAYEMS increases for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% month-over-month signals a weakening demand in the housing market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where HOUST drops by more than 10% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 25 basis points within a month signals a shift towards accommodative monetary policy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS decreases by more than 25 basis points within a month.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) growth slows to less than 1% quarter-over-quarter and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises by more than 0.3 percentage points in the same period, it signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth < 1% QoQ and UNRATE rises > 0.3pp
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where GDPC1 growth is less than 1% quarter-over-quarter and UNRATE rises by more than 0.3 percentage points.
